title: Gastric adenocarcinoma malignant programs, ecosystems and computable state reversal
question: Do recurrent malignant epithelial programs organize gastric progression and metastatic ecosystems, and can auditable virtual perturbation nominate state-shifting candidates?
target_object: malignant epithelial meta-programs linked to immune/stromal spatial niches
comparison: premalignant or adjacent versus primary versus metastatic disease; source versus desired cell state
primary_outcome: program robustness, donor-level state association, replicated spatial niche and stable perturbation candidate
claim_ceiling: cross-sectional program/ecosystem association plus computational candidate prioritization; no temporal evolution, causality or therapy efficacy without stronger evidence
falsifier: programs fail donor/cohort holdout; niche fails independent spatial replication; perturbation ranking is unstable or no better than simple baselines
anchor_reuse: multi-cohort single-cell integration; malignant programs; TME states; spatial localization; clinical projection; virtual perturbation
changed_axes: cancer type and cancer-specific states/endpoints; all anchor defects repaired rather than copied
science_basis: Public gastric cohorts cover several disease states, but the parsed GSE234129 file supports only TME and has one liver and one ovarian metastasis; a malignant-cell discovery chain and duplication boundary remain unproven.
estimated_calendar_time: 4-9 months after route qualification; unknown before full data parse
main_risk: high overlap with published gastric progression/ecotype/spatial studies plus cohort-state confounding
stop_condition: stop or reduce to partial imitation if no adequate malignant cohort, bridge design, replicated spatial data or distinct central question is found

title: Colorectal adenoma-to-carcinoma-to-liver-metastasis programs and state reversal
question: Do recurrent malignant programs connect the adenoma-carcinoma-liver-metastasis sequence to spatial ecosystems and robust computational vulnerabilities?
target_object: malignant epithelial meta-programs across precursor, primary and liver-metastatic states
comparison: normal or polyp versus primary CRC versus liver metastasis; source versus desired cell state
primary_outcome: program robustness, donor-level progression association, replicated spatial niche and stable perturbation candidate
claim_ceiling: observational continuum and computational candidate prioritization; no lineage evolution or therapeutic efficacy claim
falsifier: stage signal disappears after cohort/donor control; target question duplicates existing studies; perturbation ranking is unstable
anchor_reuse: multi-cohort single-cell integration; malignant programs; TME; spatial localization; bulk/treatment projection; virtual perturbation
changed_axes: cancer type, organ-specific progression states and endpoints; donor/stage and treatment confounding repaired
science_basis: CRC-atlas now supplies a verified public 3.79-million-cell object, parsed 650-patient/1,670-sample metadata, author code and primary spatial resources. It is the strongest next real-data candidate, but malignant cNMF, whole-transcriptome CRLM spatial validation, coherent treatment endpoints and Geneformer still require reconstruction, and near-paper overlap remains high.
estimated_calendar_time: 4-9 months after route qualification; decisive precheck can finish much earlier
main_risk: substantive repetition of CRC-atlas or existing progression/spatial-metastasis studies despite adding a new computational method
stop_condition: stop if malignant programs fail donor/cohort holdout, spatial panels cannot measure them, treatment endpoints remain incoherent, or the central question is already published
